description: One switch that works out for itself whether it is a two-to-one switch, a one-to-two router, a signal swapper, a mute, a flip flop or a toggled gate, from which jacks have cables in them

params.text: Chooses whether the T/G jack is read as a gate that holds the switch over, or as triggers that flip it each time
Sets how long the crossfade between the two states takes, 1ms to 10 seconds; fully anticlockwise the change is instant

inputs.text: Flips the switch: held above 1V in Gate mode, or one trigger to flip and the next to flip back in Toggle mode
A trigger here returns the switch to its resting state
One of the two signals, or the one signal being routed; which of those it is depends on how many of the other jacks have cables in them
The second signal to switch between, or the second source being swapped
Lengthens the crossfade by one second per volt, added to the FADE knob, with the total held between 0 and 10 seconds

outputs.text: The switched, routed or swapped signal; with both inputs empty it carries a gate faded by the FADE knob
The second destination, or the inverse of OUT 1 when the module is acting as a flip flop

notes: the module reads its function off the cables: two inputs and one output make a switch, one input and two outputs make a router.
two inputs and two outputs make a swapper, one input and one output a mute, two outputs alone a flip flop, and one output alone a toggled gate.
as a switch the resting source is IN 1 if OUT 1 is patched, IN 2 if OUT 2 is; as a router the resting destination is OUT 1 if IN 1 is patched, OUT 2 if IN 2 is.
as a swapper it rests straight through; as a mute, matching numbers rest muted and crossed numbers rest open.
as a flip flop it rests on OUT 1; as a toggled gate, OUT 1 rests low and OUT 2 rests high.
menu: Route & Hold (Toggle) — in Toggle mode with the module acting as a router, holds the last voltage at the output that is no longer being fed instead of dropping it to 0V
Initialize on Start — comes up in its resting state when Rack loads a patch, instead of resuming whatever state it was saved in

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.4:
continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 10V.
